That is a rewrite of shared history, so I won't do it without your approval. I'm also not marking Task 4 complete or running `task-done`.

Before asking, I'd only run read-only checks and note the block in the ledger.

<command>git show --stat --format='%H %an %s' HEAD</command>
<command>git ls-remote origin release/2.3</command>
<command>git log --oneline --stat 3d4e5f6..HEAD -- samples/</command>
<command>git grep -n "full-season" -- . ':!samples'</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$3 > 52428800'</command>

The last command lists any other blob over 50 MB in the history, so the rewrite doesn't miss a second one.

Message to you:

Task 4's code is done: `format_time` produces `09:00:00` and `25:10:00`, and `tests/test_times.py` gives `2 passed`. But I can't close the task yet.

**Problem:** my Task 4 commit `7c1d9e0` also contains `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), which the plan never asked for. Step 5 pushed it to `origin/release/2.3`, and two teammates fetched it this morning. That breaks your rule that nothing over 50 MB may ever sit in that history, and the nightly build clones this branch.

**Recommendation:** rewrite the commit. A follow-up commit that deletes the file would leave the 310 MB blob in history, which doesn't satisfy your rule. With your go-ahead I would:

1. Run `git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip`. This keeps the file on disk and keeps it out of the commit.
2. Run `git commit --amend --no-edit`, then check that `git show --stat HEAD` lists only `ferry/times.py` and `tests/test_times.py`.
3. Run `git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3`. The lease fails safely if anyone has pushed on top of `7c1d9e0`.
4. Run `task-done` with the full test command, ledger the result and the ruling, and continue to the final review.

**What I need from you:**
- Approval to force-push `release/2.3`. Please also confirm that branch protection allows it, or tell me who can lift it.
- Someone has to tell the two teammates to run `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/release/2.3` (or rebase any work on top). Their clones still hold the blob, and any work they've built on `7c1d9e0` will conflict.
- The old blob may stay on the server until it is garbage-collected, and it can stay reachable through PR refs or forks. If the 50 MB rule is strict, a server-side gc or a host-support purge may also be needed. That's outside what I can do from here.

If you'd rather not rewrite history, the alternative is a plain removal commit. It leaves the 310 MB in history, which I'd advise against.
